candidates.summary: No test ties the derived recoverPubkey Base to the verify row it is computed from, so a verify re-fit leaves 350,000 stale with every check green
candidates.failure_scenario: The verify row on line 129 says it must be re-fit before merge, and the recover row is defined as 1.279 x verify-at-64-bytes x 1.2. Re-fit verify on the reference machine (say its base rises to 300,000) and recoverPubkey still charges 350,000, now about 1.17x a verify instead of 1.53x, below the dense-s recovery's 1.279x worst-case measured ratio. Nothing fails: recoverPubkeyCharge only asserts the row is flat, the txtar's EXACT_GAS never calls Verify, and the fitter emits verify while skipping recoverPubkey. So validators run recoveries that cost more CPU time than the gas they charge. The same file already pins derived values this way: TestSubRealmGasMirrorsPackageAddress for packageAddress, and TestModExpRowCoversMeasuredCalibrationPoint for modexp.

candidates.summary: A recovery ID other than 0 or 1 is refused only inside the native, after the 350,000-gas flat charge, though the wrapper could refuse it beside the length check
candidates.failure_scenario: The doc comment warns about one mistake in particular: a realm that passes Ethereum's v unconverted (27/28, or an EIP-155 value). That realm pays 350,000 gas on every call to get false. The native refuses it at recover.go:21 in about 0.6 us (RefuseID, 621 ns median in secp256k1_recover_bench_m1pro.txt), roughly 560x less work than the charge. A check of signature[64] > 1 next to the len check in RecoverPubkey would return false for a few VM ops. TestRecoverPubkeyFlatCharge's 'recovery ID 2' case would then expect zero native charges.
